To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HIV-positive individuals have increased levels of cytokines in exosomes compared to healthy controls, that these exosomes can activate T cells, and that these cytokines are not present in free form but associated with exosomes.

most plasma cytokines are associated with exosomes, and exposure of naive peripheral mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to exosomes purified form HIV-positive patients induce CD38 expression on CD4(+) naive and central memory T cells, probably contribute to inflammation and viral propogation via bystander cell activiation.

exosomes purified from plasma of HIV-infected individuals were found to contain most cytokines and chemotactic factors and that exposure to exosomes purified HIV-positive individuals induced CD38 on naive and central-memory CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.
